title: The Tryton integration is small enough for a one-person shop to ship as a module
content:
The mechanism is a Tryton model hook dispatching typed operations on workflow transition. The distinctive part of this group is not the hook but the sizing judgement attached to it: the work is small enough for a one-person shop to ship as a module.

That reframes the deliverable. For larger partners the output of an integration is a reference implementation the vendor maintains; here it is a Tryton module the partner can own, publish and install for their own customers. The scope has to stay inside what a single developer can carry, which constrains the design as much as any technical requirement does.

Three leads carry this demo — Wuerfel Datentechnik, m-ds and virtual things, all German — one at "2 · next" and two at "3 · later". Small partners are usually screened out on co-build capacity, so an integration deliberately scoped to their size is the mechanism by which this part of the corpus becomes reachable at all.
